title: Area and Perimeter Formulas
seo_title: Grade 4 Area and Perimeter Formulas Worksheets (TEKS 4.5C, 4.5D, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.5C use models to determine the formulas for the perimeter of a rectangle (l + w + l + w or 2l + 2w), including the special form for perimeter of a square (4s) and the area of a rectangle (l x w); 4.5D solve problems related to perimeter and area of rectangles where dimensions are whole numbers
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 area and perimeter worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.5C and 4.5D: perimeter 2l + 2w and 4s, area l × w, missing sides, bigger numbers and L-shaped floor plans. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Perimeter: P = 2l + 2w. Area: A = l × w.
key_sub: A square has P = 4s. Area is in square units. Divide the area by one side to find the other side.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter of a rectangle: P = l + w + l + w, or P = 2l + 2w. For a square, P = 4s.
  • Area of a rectangle: A = l × w. Area is in square units.
  • To find a missing side from the area, divide: w = A ÷ l. From the perimeter, halve it and subtract the length.

Examples

Example

A rectangle is 12 ft by 7 ft. Find the perimeter and area.

P = 2 × 12 + 2 × 7 = 24 + 14 = 38 ft

A = 12 × 7 = 84 square feet

Answer: 38 ft and 84 square feet

Example

A rectangle has an area of 72 square inches and a length of 9 inches. What is the width?

72 ÷ 9 = 8

Answer: 8 inches

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using l × w for perimeterPerimeter adds all sides: 2l + 2w.
Adding only l + wThat is half the perimeter. Double it.
Writing ft for areaArea is in square units: square feet.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side?
faq.a: For area, divide the area by the known side. For perimeter, subtract the two known sides from the perimeter and halve what is left.

faq.q: How can I tell if a problem asks for area or perimeter?
faq.a: Fences, borders and trim go around: perimeter. Carpet, paint and tiles cover: area.

items.q: Jayden is covering the top of his desk with paper. What should he find?
items.e: Covering a surface means the space inside, so find the area. Area is measured in square units: sq in.

items.q: A square patio has sides of 16 ft. What is its area?
items.e: Every side of a square is 16 ft, so Area = 16 × 16 = 256 sq ft (16 × 10 = 160, 16 × 6 = 96, 160 + 96 = 256).

items.q: Diego is building a fence around a vegetable garden. What should he find?
items.e: Going along the edge means the distance around, so find the perimeter. Perimeter is a length: m, not square units.

items.q: Luis wants to hang a string of lights around the edge of a window. What should he find?
items.e: Going along the edge means the distance around, so find the perimeter. Perimeter is a length: in, not square units.

items.q: Lucia wants to buy carpet to cover her bedroom floor. What should she find?
items.e: Covering a surface means the space inside, so find the area. Area is measured in square units: sq ft.

items.q: Rectangle A is 11 cm by 5 cm. Square B has sides of 8 cm. Which is true?
c: Same area; B has more perimeter
Same perimeter; B has more area
Same area; A has more perimeter
Same perimeter; A has more area
items.e: A: area 11 × 5 = 55 sq cm, perimeter 2 × 11 + 2 × 5 = 32 cm. B: area 8 × 8 = 64 sq cm, perimeter 4 × 8 = 32 cm. Same perimeter, but the square holds more space.

items.q: Sofia is running laps around the edge of a soccer field. What should she find?
items.e: Going along the edge means the distance around, so find the perimeter. Perimeter is a length: m, not square units.

items.q: Zoe needs grass seed to cover a lawn. What should she find?
items.e: Covering a surface means the space inside, so find the area. Area is measured in square units: sq m.

items.q: A square has an area of 64 sq ft. How long is each side?
items.e: Find the number that times itself makes 64: 8 × 8 = 64. Each side is 8 ft. (Dividing by 4 works for perimeter, not area.)

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 100 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm. Check: 4 × 25 = 100. (10 × 10 = 100 is an area, not a perimeter.)

items.q: Rectangle A is 9 ft by 4 ft. Square B has sides of 6 ft. Which is true?
c: Same area; A has more perimeter
Same perimeter; B has more area
Same perimeter; A has more area
Same area; B has more perimeter
items.e: A: area 9 × 4 = 36 sq ft, perimeter 2 × 9 + 2 × 4 = 26 ft. B: area 6 × 6 = 36 sq ft, perimeter 4 × 6 = 24 ft. Same area, but the long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: A square picture has sides of 18 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 18 = 72 cm.

items.q: This is a square. What is its area?
items.e: Every side of a square is 13 m, so Area = 13 × 13 = 169 sq m (13 × 10 = 130, 13 × 3 = 39, 130 + 39 = 169).

c: Same area; B has more perimeter

items.e: A: area 10 × 4 = 40 sq m, perimeter 2 × 10 + 2 × 4 = 28 m. B: area 7 × 7 = 49 sq m, perimeter 4 × 7 = 28 m. Same perimeter, but the square holds more space.

items.q: A square has an area of 144 sq in. How long is each side?
items.e: Find the number that times itself makes 144: 12 × 12 = 144. Each side is 12 in. (Dividing by 4 works for perimeter, not area.)

c: Same area; B has more perimeter
Same perimeter; A has more area
Same perimeter; B has more area
Same area; A has more perimeter
items.e: A: area 16 × 4 = 64 sq in, perimeter 2 × 16 + 2 × 4 = 40 in. B: area 8 × 8 = 64 sq in, perimeter 4 × 8 = 32 in. Same area, but the long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: A rectangle is 10 in long and 9 in wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 10 × 9 = 90 sq in. Area counts squares, so the unit is sq in. (38 is the perimeter.)

items.e: Area = length × width = 9 × 8 = 72 sq cm. Area counts squares, so the unit is sq cm. (34 is the perimeter.)

items.q: This is a square. What is its area?

items.q: A rectangle is 7 ft long and 4 ft wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 7 + 2 × 4 = 14 + 8 = 22 ft. Adding only 7 + 4 = 11 leaves out two sides.

items.q: A rectangle is 11 ft long and 9 ft wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 11 + 2 × 9 = 22 + 18 = 40 ft. Adding only 11 + 9 = 20 leaves out two sides.

items.q: A rectangle is 9 in long and 3 in wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 9 × 3 = 27 sq in. Area counts squares, so the unit is sq in. (24 is the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle is 8 in long and 7 in wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 8 × 7 = 56 sq in. Area counts squares, so the unit is sq in. (30 is the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle is 5 ft long and 2 ft wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 5 + 2 × 2 = 10 + 4 = 14 ft. Adding only 5 + 2 = 7 leaves out two sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 12 + 2 × 9 = 24 + 18 = 42 m. Adding only 12 + 9 = 21 leaves out two sides.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 26 m. It is 10 m long. Which equation can you use to find the width, w?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width, so 2 × 10 + 2 × w = 26. 20 + 2 × w = 26, 2 × w = 6, w = 3 m.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 44 in. It is 12 in long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 12 = 24. 44 − 24 = 20 for the two widths, so each width is 20 ÷ 2 = 10 in. Check: 12 + 10 + 12 + 10 = 44.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 126 sq ft. Its length is 7 ft. What is its width?
items.e: Think of the area formula with a missing factor: 7 × ? = 126. Divide: 126 ÷ 7 = 18 ft. Check: 7 × 18 = 126.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 40 sq cm. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 8 × ? = 40. 40 ÷ 8 = 5, so the side is 5 cm. Check: 8 × 5 = 40.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 48 sq cm. It is 12 cm long. Which equation can you use to find the width, w?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 12 × w = 48. Then w = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 cm.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 96 sq m. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 8 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 8 = 12, so the side is 12 m. Check: 8 × 12 = 96.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 58 in. What is the width marked ?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 16 = 32. 58 − 32 = 26 for the two widths, so each width is 26 ÷ 2 = 13 in. Check: 16 + 13 + 16 + 13 = 58.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 108 sq in. Its length is 9 in. What is its width?
items.e: Think of the area formula with a missing factor: 9 × ? = 108. Divide: 108 ÷ 9 = 12 in. Check: 9 × 12 = 108.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 60 sq ft. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 6 × ? = 60. 60 ÷ 6 = 10, so the side is 10 ft. Check: 6 × 10 = 60.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 156 sq m. Its width is 6 m. What is its length?
items.e: Think of the area formula with a missing factor: 6 × ? = 156. Divide: 156 ÷ 6 = 26 m. Check: 6 × 26 = 156.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 62 m. It is 19 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 19 = 38. 62 − 38 = 24 for the two widths, so each width is 24 ÷ 2 = 12 m. Check: 19 + 12 + 19 + 12 = 62.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 42 ft. It is 14 ft long. Which equation can you use to find the width, w?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width, so 2 × 14 + 2 × w = 42. 28 + 2 × w = 42, 2 × w = 14, w = 7 ft.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 56 sq cm. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 8 × ? = 56. 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so the side is 7 cm. Check: 8 × 7 = 56.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 40 cm. What is the width marked ?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 11 = 22. 40 − 22 = 18 for the two widths, so each width is 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm. Check: 11 + 9 + 11 + 9 = 40.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 50 sq m. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 5 × ? = 50. 50 ÷ 5 = 10, so the side is 10 m. Check: 5 × 10 = 50.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 96 sq cm. Its width is 8 cm. What is its length?
items.e: Think of the area formula with a missing factor: 8 × ? = 96. Divide: 96 ÷ 8 = 12 cm. Check: 8 × 12 = 96.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 108 sq in. It is 12 in long. Which equation can you use to find the width, w?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 12 × w = 108. Then w = 108 ÷ 12 = 9 in.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 62 ft. It is 18 ft long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 18 = 36. 62 − 36 = 26 for the two widths, so each width is 26 ÷ 2 = 13 ft. Check: 18 + 13 + 18 + 13 = 62.

items.q: The area of the rectangle is 32 sq in. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 8 × ? = 32. 32 ÷ 8 = 4, so the side is 4 in. Check: 8 × 4 = 32.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 40 ft. What is the width marked ?
items.e: The two lengths are 2 × 13 = 26. 40 − 26 = 14 for the two widths, so each width is 14 ÷ 2 = 7 ft. Check: 13 + 7 + 13 + 7 = 40.

sets.title: Bigger numbers and the right formula

items.q: A farmer puts a fence around a field that is 35 meters long and 18 meters wide. Which equation finds the length of the fence?
items.e: Going around the edge is perimeter: 2 lengths + 2 widths = 70 + 36 = 106 m. 35 × 18 finds the area inside.

items.q: A painter covers a wall that is 42 feet wide and 25 feet tall. Which equation finds how much wall gets painted?
items.e: Covering a surface is area, so multiply length × width: A = 42 × 25 = 1,050 sq ft. The perimeter equation finds the distance around.

items.q: A runner jogs once around a parking lot that is 36 meters long and 23 meters wide. Which equation finds how far the runner goes?
items.e: Going around the edge is perimeter: 2 lengths + 2 widths = 72 + 46 = 118 m. 36 × 23 finds the area inside.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 34 × 24 = 816 sq in (34 × 20 = 680, 34 × 4 = 136, 680 + 136 = 816). Multiply every part: 34 × 24 is not only 30 × 20 plus 4 × 4.

items.q: A school puts mats on a gym floor that is 17 feet long and 14 feet wide. Which equation finds how much floor the mats cover?
items.e: Covering a surface is area, so multiply length × width: A = 17 × 14 = 238 sq ft. The perimeter equation finds the distance around.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 45 + 2 × 18 = 90 + 36 = 126 m. Or add first: 45 + 18 = 63, then 2 × 63 = 126 m.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 27 + 2 × 23 = 54 + 46 = 100 ft. Or add first: 27 + 23 = 50, then 2 × 50 = 100 ft.

items.q: A family buys carpet for a floor that is 27 feet long and 26 feet wide. Which equation finds how much carpet covers the floor?
items.e: Covering a surface is area, so multiply length × width: A = 27 × 26 = 702 sq ft. The perimeter equation finds the distance around.

items.q: A rectangle is 35 in long and 16 in wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 35 × 16 = 560 sq in (35 × 10 = 350, 35 × 6 = 210, 350 + 210 = 560). Multiply every part: 35 × 16 is not only 30 × 10 plus 5 × 6.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 47 + 2 × 29 = 94 + 58 = 152 ft. Or add first: 47 + 29 = 76, then 2 × 76 = 152 ft.

items.q: A rectangle is 37 ft long and 24 ft wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 37 + 2 × 24 = 74 + 48 = 122 ft. Or add first: 37 + 24 = 61, then 2 × 61 = 122 ft.

items.q: A tailor sews lace along every edge of a pillow cover that is 35 inches long and 28 inches wide. Which equation finds the length of the lace?
items.e: Going around the edge is perimeter: 2 lengths + 2 widths = 70 + 56 = 126 in. 35 × 28 finds the area inside.

items.q: A rectangle is 37 m long and 13 m wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 37 + 2 × 13 = 74 + 26 = 100 m. Or add first: 37 + 13 = 50, then 2 × 50 = 100 m.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 38 × 15 = 570 sq in (38 × 10 = 380, 38 × 5 = 190, 380 + 190 = 570). Multiply every part: 38 × 15 is not only 30 × 10 plus 8 × 5.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 39 × 28 = 1,092 sq cm (39 × 20 = 780, 39 × 8 = 312, 780 + 312 = 1,092). Multiply every part: 39 × 28 is not only 30 × 20 plus 9 × 8.

items.q: A class glues a paper border around a bulletin board that is 19 inches long and 17 inches tall. Which equation finds the length of the border?
items.e: Going around the edge is perimeter: 2 lengths + 2 widths = 38 + 34 = 72 in. 19 × 17 finds the area inside.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 45 + 2 × 16 = 90 + 32 = 122 m. Or add first: 45 + 16 = 61, then 2 × 61 = 122 m.

items.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width = 27 × 16 = 432 sq cm (27 × 10 = 270, 27 × 6 = 162, 270 + 162 = 432). Multiply every part: 27 × 16 is not only 20 × 10 plus 7 × 6.

items.q: A rectangle is 36 cm long and 27 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 36 × 27 = 972 sq cm (36 × 20 = 720, 36 × 7 = 252, 720 + 252 = 972). Multiply every part: 36 × 27 is not only 30 × 20 plus 6 × 7.

items.q: A park plants grass on a lawn that is 22 meters long and 15 meters wide. Which equation finds the area of grass?
items.e: Covering a surface is area, so multiply length × width: A = 22 × 15 = 330 sq m. The perimeter equation finds the distance around.

items.q: Camila's room is 14 feet long and 11 feet wide. She puts baseboard along the bottom of every wall, except for a doorway that is 3 feet wide. How much baseboard does she need?
items.e: Perimeter: 2 × 14 + 2 × 11 = 50 ft. No baseboard goes across the doorway: 50 − 3 = 47 ft.

items.q: This is the shape of an L-shaped garden. What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: The two shorter sides going across, ? and 7 m, together match the long 16 m side. 16 − 7 = 9 m.

items.q: A rectangular dog park has an area of 240 square meters. It is 20 meters long. How many meters of fence go around the park?
items.e: Step 1: width = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 m. Step 2: perimeter = 2 × 20 + 2 × 12 = 40 + 24 = 64 m. (12 m is only the width, not the fence.)

items.q: This is the floor plan of a room. Think of a 14 by 7 rectangle with a corner cut out. What is its area?
items.e: Big rectangle 14 × 7 = 98, minus the cut-out corner 8 × 3 = 24: 98 − 24 = 74 sq ft. Check: split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 8 × 4 = 32. Add: 42 + 32 = 74 sq ft.

items.q: Gabriel used 86 feet of fence to go around a rectangular garden. The garden is 25 feet long. How wide is it?
items.e: Two lengths: 2 × 25 = 50. 86 − 50 = 36 for the two widths. 36 ÷ 2 = 18 ft.

items.q: A school playground is 45 meters long and 32 meters wide. What is its area?
A swimming pool is 25 meters long and 12 meters wide. A cover goes over the whole pool. What is the area of the cover?
items.e: Area = length × width = 25 × 12 = 300 sq m (25 × 10 = 250, 25 × 2 = 50, 250 + 50 = 300). The cover spreads over the whole surface, so this is area.

items.q: This is a piece of cardboard cut for a model. The dashed line splits it into two rectangles. What is its area?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 7 × 9 = 63 and 9 × 5 = 45. Add: 63 + 45 = 108 sq cm. Check: big rectangle 16 × 9 = 144, minus the cut-out corner 9 × 4 = 36: 144 − 36 = 108 sq cm.

items.q: This is the shape of a patio. The dashed line splits it into two rectangles. What is its area?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 9 = 72 and 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 72 + 28 = 100 sq ft. Check: big rectangle 15 × 9 = 135, minus the cut-out corner 7 × 5 = 35: 135 − 35 = 100 sq ft.

items.q: This is the floor plan of a kitchen. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all 6 sides: 6 + 3 + 7 + 4 + 13 + 7 = 40 ft. Do not skip the two short sides at the cut-out corner.

items.q: This is the shape of a wooden deck. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all 6 sides: 6 + 4 + 7 + 5 + 13 + 9 = 44 ft. Do not skip the two short sides at the cut-out corner.

items.q: This is the shape of a swimming area at a lake. The dashed line splits it into two rectangles. What is its area?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 49 + 15 = 64 sq m. Check: big rectangle 12 × 7 = 84, minus the cut-out corner 5 × 4 = 20: 84 − 20 = 64 sq m.

items.q: Diego's backyard is 30 feet long and 20 feet wide. A patio that is 10 feet by 8 feet is in the yard. The rest is grass. What is the area of the grass?
items.e: Whole yard: 30 × 20 = 600 sq ft. Patio: 10 × 8 = 80 sq ft. Grass: 600 − 80 = 520 sq ft.

items.q: A rectangular bedroom has 132 square feet of flooring. The room is 12 feet long. How wide is the room?
items.e: Area = length × width, so 12 × ? = 132. 132 ÷ 12 = 11. The room is 11 feet wide.

items.q: This is the shape of a skate park. Think of a 9 by 7 rectangle with a corner cut out. What is its area?
items.e: Big rectangle 9 × 7 = 63, minus the cut-out corner 5 × 4 = 20: 63 − 20 = 43 sq m. Check: split it into two rectangles: 4 × 7 = 28 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 28 + 15 = 43 sq m.

items.q: Sofia builds a fence around a rectangular garden that is 18 meters long and 11 meters wide. How many meters of fence does she need?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width = 2 × 18 + 2 × 11 = 36 + 22 = 58 m. The fence goes along all 4 sides.

items.q: A coach runs around a rectangular field 2 times. The field is 90 meters long and 60 meters wide. How far does the coach run?
items.e: Once around: 2 × 90 + 2 × 60 = 300 m. Two times around: 2 × 300 = 600 m.

items.q: Caleb covers a laundry room floor that is 9 feet by 8 feet with square tiles. Each tile is 1 square foot and costs $3. How much do the tiles cost?
items.e: Step 1: area = 9 × 8 = 72 sq ft, so 72 tiles. Step 2: cost = 72 × $3 = $216.

items.q: Ximena puts ribbon around the edge of a poster that is 36 inches tall and 24 inches wide. How much ribbon does she need?
items.e: Ribbon goes around the edge, so find the perimeter: 2 × 36 + 2 × 24 = 72 + 48 = 120 inches. (864 sq in is the area of the poster.)

items.q: A soccer field is 100 meters long and 64 meters wide. What is the area of the field?
items.e: Area = 100 × 64 = 6,400 sq m. Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros after 64.
